verifiedBehavior: One reviewed action and original actor/company/target, durable prepare and one-use dispatch in separate physical SQL commits; no SQL transaction across Graph.
Acknowledged additions/removals stay pending; a separate current observation confirms actual direct effect and preserves the original pending attempt.
Unknown additions neither establish ownership nor automatically resend; old operation IDs return only their original retained outcome.
Fresh source expiry at actual prepare/dispatch commits prevents POST; expiry after POST still retains the original workload receipt while denying private success.
Changed reviewed action, recipient state, operator configuration or canonical group membership prevents a new write.
Definite throttles retain bounded wait; ambiguous transport/server failures remain unknown, even with a supplied false uncertainty flag.
Concurrent target requests cannot dispatch twice; the held SQL client checks original state without requesting a second connection from an exhausted pool.
External group/direct licenses remain retained; source overlap and desired-state reversal do not cause an automatic compensating POST.
Metadata retirement/reapplication, mounted HTTP routes, workload history and absent configuration are checked against real disposable PostgreSQL.
Dedicated legacy role cannot execute company metadata or delivery functions; raw token and nonce do not appear in retained operations.
providerBoundary: All new Graph responses, token acquisition and mutations use explicit in-process provider fixtures. Local metadata, license sources, SQL transactions, deferred commit guards and HTTP routes use actual PostgreSQL. This does not verify a real Microsoft tenant or execute a company write through the actual Rust CLI.
browserBoundary: The earlier actual unconfigured TOTP/browser case is recorded in company-microsoft-preview-2026-11-16.json. Configured provider browser coverage was not run for this checkpoint.
remaining: Explicit fresh-human recovery after process loss without reconstructing an old nonce or permitting redispatch.
Explicit review/adoption/retry decision bound to the original uncertain addition; no automatic ownership acquisition.
Configured provider browser flow and actual Microsoft test tenant consent, mappings and observed effect.
Final full Linux CI, release/backup/migration validation and deployment.
